'''Gustav Andreas Tammann''' (24 July 1932 – 6 January 2019) was a Swiss [[astronomer]] and academic. He served as director of the Astronomical Institute of the [[University of Basel]]; as a member of the [[European Space Agency]] [[Space Telescope]] Advisory Team, and as Member of Council of the [[European Southern Observatory]]. His research interests included [[supernovae]] and the [[galaxy|extragalactic]] distance scale. Tammann was a former President of the [[International Astronomical Union]] Commission on Galaxies.

Tammann is the grandson of chemist-physicist [[Gustav Heinrich Tammann]].<ref name=S />

==Education and early career==
Tammann studied astronomy in [[Basel]], [[Switzerland]] and [[Göttingen]], [[Germany]]. In 1963 he began a longtime working relationship with [[Allan Rex Sandage|Allan Sandage]] at the Mount Wilson and Palomar observatories.<ref name=AG>{{cite web |url= https://astronomische-gesellschaft.de/en/member/obituaries/prof-dr-gustav-andreas-tammann-1932-2019  |title= Prof. Dr. Gustav Andreas Tammann (1932-2019)|author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Astronomische Gesellschaft |publisher= |access-date= April 28, 2025|quote=}}</ref>

==Academic career==
In 1972, he became a professor at the [[University of Hamburg]].<ref name=S>{{cite web |url= https://sps.ch/en/articles/obituaries/gustav_andreas_tammann |title= In Memoriam Gustav Andreas Tammann |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Swiss Physical Society |publisher= |access-date= April 28, 2025|quote=}}</ref> From 1977 until his retirement, he was a professor and head of the Astronomical Institute at the [[University of Basel]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.eso.org/sci/publications/messenger/archive/no.176-jun19/messenger-no176-58-58.pdf |title= Gustav Andreas Tammann (1932–2019) |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= European Southern Observatory |publisher= |access-date= April 28, 2025|quote=}}</ref>  

His work focused mainly on the determination of the [[Hubble]] constant as well as the use of supernovae as cosmic distance indicators.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://baas.aas.org/pub/2020i0303/release/1 |title= Gustav Andreas Tammann (1932–2019)|author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= American Astronomical Society |publisher= |access-date= April 28, 2025|quote=}}</ref>  

==Accolades==
In 1991 Tammann became a full member of [[Academia Europaea]], and in 1993 became a [[corresponding member]] of the [[Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Member of HAdW|url=http://www.haw.uni-heidelberg.de/akademie/member.en.html?id=211|website=haw.uni-heidelberg.de|accessdate=8 April 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160803221952/http://www.haw.uni-heidelberg.de/akademie/member.en.html?id=211|archivedate=3 August 2016|language=German|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2000 he received the [[Albert Einstein Medal]] that is given for "outstanding scientific findings, works, or publications related to Albert Einstein"<ref name="urlAlbert Einstein Medal">{{cite web
|url=http://www.nndb.com/honors/166/000115818/|title=Albert Einstein Medal|accessdate=2010-10-27}}</ref> and the [[Tomalla Foundation|Tomalla Prize]] for his efforts in measuring the expansion rate of the universe and especially for his pioneering work using Supernovae as standard candles.<ref name="urlThe Tomalla Foundation">{{cite web
|url=http://www.tomalla.ch/prize_winner.htm|title=The Tomalla Foundation|accessdate=2010-10-27}}</ref> In 2005 he received the [[Karl Schwarzschild Medal]].<ref name=AG />

The asteroid [[18872 Tammann]] was named for him in 2001.<ref name="urlJPL Small-Body Database Browser">{{cite web
|url=http://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.cgi?sstr=18872+Tammann
|title=Main-belt Asteroid: 18872 Tammann (1999 VR20)
|accessdate=2010-10-27
}}</ref>
